clinician.trajectory_summary: A 2-year-old boy presented to the emergency department with acute onset of extremely painful bilateral non-pitting edema of both hands and purpuric lesions on the left cheek, nostril, and ear. The child was afebrile with no preceding trauma. On admission, laboratory evaluation revealed normal blood cell count, elevated inflammatory markers (CRP 14.2 mg/dL, ESR 110 mm/hr), and negative urinalysis. During observation, the edema and purpuric lesions progressively spread to the arms, feet, and legs. The patient was treated with ibuprofen and experienced complete resolution of all lesions within 72 hours. The clinical presentation, age (2 years), characteristic distribution of cutaneous involvement (facial purpura with bilateral hand edema spreading to extremities), laboratory findings (normal CBC, elevated inflammatory markers, negative urinalysis ruling out renal involvement), and rapid self-limited response to treatment are all consistent with acute hemorrhagic edema of infancy (AHE).
